incident-bot: PAGER: SLO_BREACH streaming-api-prod — p95 ~730ms (SLO 300ms), p99 ~2.1s (SLO 1s). Symptoms: streaming stalls, tail decode spikes. Metric spike correlates with KV cache eviction_rate and prefill failures. Investigate.
Alice Ramos: ack, I'm on it. grabbing dashboards now. pinging infra team in case we need capacity.
Bob Chen: seeing the same. KV_eviction_rate spiked ~3x at 21:02 UTC, and kv_fragmentation metric jumped. Could be prefill vs decode imbalance — prefill thundering leading to decode workers blocking.
Carla K: noted increased queuing on decode workers (cpu wait). Streaming sessions show long gaps between server-sent events.
Alice Ramos: quick mitigation idea: lower prefill concurrency and raise eviction threshold to avoid aggressive thrash. Also can route a small % of traffic to standby region.
Dave S: agree. I'm ready to scale up decode pool if needed. what's safe for memory?
Bob Chen: memory headroom on decode nodes ~12% currently. If we scale, we risk more evictions. Better to reduce prefill concurrency first.
Alice Ramos: running a conservative change: set runtime.prefill.max_concurrency=0.6 -> 0.3 for streaming-prod. Applying via runbook cmd.
Carla K: add the command please so I can follow.
Alice Ramos: running: 
```
# reduce prefill concurrency on streaming-prod
redwoodctl runtime patch-config --pool streaming-prod --set 'prefill.max_concurrency=0.3'
```
incident-bot: CONFIG_CHANGE applied by Alice Ramos at 21:06 UTC: prefill.max_concurrency=0.3
Bob Chen: also toggling eviction_policy favor_recent to reduce fragmentation evictions. Command: 
```
redwoodctl runtime patch-config --pool streaming-prod --set 'kv.eviction_policy=favor_recent'
```
Dave S: I'll start a +2 decode node scale to absorb current inflight decodes. starting now.
deploy-bot: autoscaler: scale up requested by Dave S -> +2 nodes (decode-pool). expected up in ~90s.
Carla K: checking live logs: saw several decode worker 504s when attempting to fetch KV prefix, lots of repeated prefill attempts.  Repeated prefill + eviction loop looks likely.
Bob Chen: I'm running a quick KV stats query: 
```
# kv cache stats snapshot
redwoodctl metrics query 'kv_cache.evictions_rate[5m], kv_cache.prefill_attempts[5m], kv_cache.prefill_failures[5m]'
```
Bob Chen: results: eviction_rate=0.32/s (baseline 0.1/s), prefill_attempts spike 4x, prefill_failures=27% during spike window.
Alice Ramos: customer impact: streaming API error rate up ~0.6% overall, but p99 latency increased causing timeouts for long-poll apps. Not seeing elevated token-cost anomalies.
Carla K: flagged major customer AcmeCorp (prod) saw 4 timeouts in the past 15m — support alerted.
Bob Chen: mitigation status: prefill conc dropped, eviction_policy changed, decode pool scale started. Metrics trending: p95 dropped to ~420ms within 6m of config change. p99 still ~1.4s, improving.
Dave S: decode nodes healthy, new nodes joined cluster at +110s. No crash loops. CPU utilization across decode pool down ~15%.
Alice Ramos: long-term followup items: consider prefill backpressure circuit breaker, better KV fragmentation metrics, and a tuned prefill backoff algorithm. I'll log a JIRA.
Carla K: agree — also need a synthetic test that exercises prefill-heavy patterns to catch this in staging.
Bob Chen: for now, I'm leaving an automated fallback rule: if eviction_rate > 0.25/s for >5m, automatically reduce prefill.max_concurrency by 25% and notify oncall. Deploying rule.
incident-bot: ALERT_FALLBACK_RULE_UPDATED by Bob Chen at 21:18 UTC: prefill_autothrottle enabled.
Alice Ramos: handoff — my shift ends in ~20m. Bob, can you take next-stage oncall please? I'll summarize: root cause likely prefill/decode imbalance causing KV thrash and tail stalls; mitigations applied: lower prefill concurrency, favor_recent eviction, +2 decode nodes. Monitoring for 30m, then revert changes if stable.
Bob Chen: taking handoff. I'll keep watch for 45m and escalate to infra if eviction_rate doesn't fall below 0.12/s. Thanks.
Carla K: leaving notes: JIRA INFRA-1789 created "prefill backpressure + kv-frag mitigations" with preliminary blameless RCA items.
Dave S: adding runbook snippet to ops repo for future: 
```
# Mitigation checklist for KV thrash-induced latency
1) reduce prefill.max_concurrency to 0.3
2) set kv.eviction_policy=favor_recent
3) scale decode pool +1..+3 as needed
4) enable prefill_autothrottle fallback
5) notify customers via support if timeouts exceed 0.1% for >15m
```
incident-bot: INCIDENT: monitoring for SLO recovery. If p99 < 1s and eviction_rate < 0.12/s for 30m, incident will auto-close.
Bob Chen: current live numbers (21:28 UTC): p95=310ms, p99=980ms, eviction_rate=0.09/s. Looks like we're back under SLO.
Alice Ramos: great work — I'll post a short summary to #incidents after handoff. Bob, please escalate if anything regresses.
Bob Chen: will do. closing my watch in 40m unless otherwise.
incident-bot: INCIDENT_CLOSED condition met at 21:32 UTC (auto-close criteria satisfied).
